findings.title: setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException and breaks client deletion in V2
findings.body: AdminPermissions.registerListener (unchanged in behavior, services/.../AdminPermissions.java line 91) calls management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent whenever the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is enabled. With this PR, when the V2 feature is on, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled (and isPermissionsEnabled) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). The exception is thrown from a ProviderEventListener during client removal, so deleting any client in a realm with admin fine-grained authz V2 enabled will fail/roll back. The V2 implementation should no-op these legacy methods instead of throwing.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException when the 'Clients' all-resource does not exist
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no per-client resource is found, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE), which returns null when the resource named 'Clients' is absent from the resource server (getResourceTypeResource returns null if resourceStore.findByName finds nothing). The result is passed directly into authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check, which will NPE instead of returning false. Contrast with hasPermission(String) a few lines below, which does check for null before evaluating. A missing or corrupted 'Clients' resource therefore turns every client permission check into a 500 error.
